claim: CRISPR prime editing (PE) requires a Cas9 nickase-reverse transcriptase fusion protein (known as PE2) and a prime editing guide RNA (pegRNA).
source: CRISPR prime editing (PE) requires a Cas9 nickase-reverse transcriptase fusion protein (known as PE2) and a prime editing guide RNA (pegRNA), an extended version of a standard guide RNA (gRNA) that both specifies the intended target genomic sequence and encodes the desired genetic edit.
evidence: This is a definitional statement about PE technology that is established knowledge in the field.

claim: pegRNA is an extended version of a standard guide RNA (gRNA) that both specifies the intended target genomic sequence and encodes the desired genetic edit.
source: CRISPR prime editing (PE) requires a Cas9 nickase-reverse transcriptase fusion protein (known as PE2) and a prime editing guide RNA (pegRNA), an extended version of a standard guide RNA (gRNA) that both specifies the intended target genomic sequence and encodes the desired genetic edit.
evidence: This is a definitional statement about pegRNA structure and function that is established knowledge.

claim: Sequence complementarity between the 5' and the 3' regions of a pegRNA can negatively impact its ability to complex with Cas9.
source: Here, we show that sequence complementarity between the 5' and the 3' regions of a pegRNA can negatively impact its ability to complex with Cas9, thereby potentially reducing PE efficiency.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from in vitro competition assays and zebrafish experiments shown in Figure 1.

claim: Sequence complementarity between the 5' and the 3' regions of a pegRNA can potentially reduce PE efficiency.
source: Here, we show that sequence complementarity between the 5' and the 3' regions of a pegRNA can negatively impact its ability to complex with Cas9, thereby potentially reducing PE efficiency.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that reduced Cas9 binding leads to reduced editing efficiency.

claim: A simple pegRNA refolding procedure can improve ribonucleoprotein-mediated PE efficiencies in zebrafish embryos by up to nearly 25-fold.
source: We demonstrate this limitation can be overcome by a simple pegRNA refolding procedure, which improved ribonucleoprotein-mediated PE efficiencies in zebrafish embryos by up to nearly 25-fold.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2.

claim: Introducing point mutations designed to disrupt internal interactions within the pegRNA can achieve further gains in PE efficiencies of as much as sixfold.
source: Further gains in PE efficiencies of as much as sixfold could also be achieved by introducing point mutations designed to disrupt internal interactions within the pegRNA.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2c and 2d.

claim: PE enables programmable installation of any nucleotide substitution and small insertions/deletions without requiring a DNA donor template or the introduction of DNA double-strand breaks.
source: PE is a versatile gene-editing technology that enables programmable installation of any nucleotide substitution and small insertions/deletions without requiring a DNA donor template or the introduction of DNA double-strand breaks (Anzalone et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Anzalone et al., 2020.

claim: PE utilizes a Cas9 nickase (nCas9)-reverse transcriptase (RT) fusion protein called PE2 and a prime editing guide RNA (pegRNA).
source: It utilizes a Cas9 nickase (nCas9)-reverse transcriptase (RT) fusion protein called PE2 and a prime editing guide RNA (pegRNA, Figure 1a).
evidence: This is a definitional statement about PE components that is established knowledge and illustrated in Figure 1a.

claim: The pegRNA directs nCas9 to the target DNA site specified by the 5' spacer sequence.
source: Like a gRNA, the pegRNA directs nCas9 to the target DNA site specified by the 5' spacer sequence.
evidence: This is established knowledge about how pegRNA functions in PE.

claim: The non-target DNA strand nicked by nCas9 anneals to a complementary primer binding site (PBS) at the 3' end of the pegRNA.
source: The non-target DNA strand nicked by nCas9 then anneals to a complementary primer binding site (PBS) at the 3' end of the pegRNA.
evidence: This describes the mechanism of PE based on established knowledge.

claim: The reverse transcriptase template (RTT) encoded in the pegRNA is reverse transcribed by the PE2 RT generating a 3' DNA 'flap' that encodes the desired edit.
source: Subsequently, the adjacent reverse transcriptase template (RTT) also encoded in the pegRNA is reverse transcribed by the PE2 RT generating a 3' DNA 'flap' that encodes the desired edit (Anzalone et al., 2019).
evidence: This describes the mechanism of PE supported by citation to Anzalone et al., 2019.

claim: PE has been successfully employed in mammalian cells, plants, Drosophila, zebrafish and mice.
source: Although PE has been successfully employed in mammalian cells, plants, Drosophila, zebrafish and mice, the editing efficiencies observed are generally lower than those observed with other forms of CRISPR/Cas-based editing (e.g. nucleases and base editors; Anzalone et al., 2019; Bosch et al., 2021; Petri et al., 2022; Lin et al., 2020; Liu et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to prior work.

claim: The editing efficiencies observed with PE are generally lower than those observed with other forms of CRISPR/Cas-based editing (e.g. nucleases and base editors).
source: Although PE has been successfully employed in mammalian cells, plants, Drosophila, zebrafish and mice, the editing efficiencies observed are generally lower than those observed with other forms of CRISPR/Cas-based editing (e.g. nucleases and base editors; Anzalone et al., 2019; Bosch et al., 2021; Petri et al., 2022; Lin et al., 2020; Liu et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to prior work.

claim: Lower indel frequencies were observed with pegRNAs than with their matched gRNAs across all six target spacer sites tested in zebrafish embryos.
source: We found that across all six target spacer sites, lower indel frequencies were observed with pegRNAs than with their matched gRNAs (Figure 1b), suggesting that the presence of the 3' extension in a pegRNA decreases Cas9-induced gene editing.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1b.

claim: The presence of the 3' extension in a pegRNA decreases Cas9-induced gene editing.
source: We found that across all six target spacer sites, lower indel frequencies were observed with pegRNAs than with their matched gRNAs (Figure 1b), suggesting that the presence of the 3' extension in a pegRNA decreases Cas9-induced gene editing.
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental observation that pegRNAs show lower indel frequencies than matched gRNAs.

claim: Interactions between complementary sequences in the 5' spacer and 3' PBS and RTT might cause misfolding of pegRNAs in a way that decreases their abilities to complex with Cas9 protein.
source: One potential explanation for the lower Cas9 activities we observed with pegRNAs compared with standard gRNAs is that interactions between complementary sequences in the 5' spacer and 3' PBS and RTT might cause misfolding of pegRNAs in a way that decreases their abilities to complex with Cas9 protein (Figure 1c).
evidence: This is a hypothesis proposed by the authors and illustrated in Figure 1c.

claim: Internal interactions between bases in standard gRNAs can stabilize alternative non-functional folding and low SpCas9-induced mutation efficiencies.
source: This possibility seemed likely given that previous work has shown that even shorter length internal interactions between bases in standard gRNAs can stabilize alternative non-functional folding and low SpCas9-induced mutation efficiencies (Thyme et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Thyme et al., 2016.

claim: In all four cases tested, gRNAs could efficiently compete with the EGFP-targeted gRNA for binding to Cas9, whereas the pegRNAs were substantially and significantly reduced in this capability.
source: Using this assay, we compared matched gRNAs and pegRNAs targeted to four different genomic DNA sites, gpr78a, adgrf3b, cacng2b and gpr85 and found that in all four cases the gRNAs could efficiently compete with the EGFP-targeted gRNA for binding to Cas9 (as judged by reduced cleavage of the EGFP DNA target site template), whereas the pegRNAs were substantially and significantly reduced in this capability (Figure 1e and f; Figure 1—source data 1 and 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1e and f.

claim: Introducing three point mutations in the 3' PBS region of pegRNAs showed significant increases in their competitive Cas9-binding activities.
source: To test whether this reduced Cas9-binding capability of the pegRNAs might be caused in part by their 5' vs 3' complementarity, we performed additional in vitro experiments with matched pegRNAs in which we introduced three point mutations in the 3' PBS region of the pegRNAs (Figure 1—source data 3) and found that these mutated pegRNAs showed significant increases in their competitive Cas9-binding activities (Figure 1e and f; Figure 1—source data 1 and 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1e and f.

claim: Refolding low-activity gRNAs believed to have alternative folding configurations can significantly improve their abilities to mediate Cas9-induced indels.
source: We considered this hypothesis because it has been previously shown that refolding low-activity gRNAs believed to have alternative folding configurations can significantly improve their abilities to mediate Cas9-induced indels (Thyme et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Thyme et al., 2016.

claim: Subjecting pegRNAs to a refolding procedure consisting of heat denaturation followed by slow cooling significantly improved their abilities to bind Cas9 in the in vitro DNA cleavage competition assay.
source: We found that subjecting pegRNAs to a refolding procedure consisting of heat denaturation followed by slow cooling (Materials and methods) significantly improved their abilities to bind Cas9 in the in vitro DNA cleavage competition assay (although not to levels observed with matched standard gRNAs Figure 1e and f; Figure 1—source data 1 and 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1e and f.

claim: Refolded pegRNAs did not reach Cas9-binding levels observed with matched standard gRNAs.
source: We found that subjecting pegRNAs to a refolding procedure consisting of heat denaturation followed by slow cooling (Materials and methods) significantly improved their abilities to bind Cas9 in the in vitro DNA cleavage competition assay (although not to levels observed with matched standard gRNAs Figure 1e and f; Figure 1—source data 1 and 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1e and f.

claim: Re-folding of pegRNAs prior to formation and injection of pegRNA-Cas9 ribonucleoprotein complexes into zebrafish embryos increased Cas9-mediated indel frequencies by up to 2.8-fold for four of the seven target sites tested.
source: Consistent with this, we also observed that re-folding of pegRNAs prior to formation and injection of pegRNA-Cas9 ribonucleoprotein complexes into zebrafish embryos also increased Cas9-mediated indel frequencies by up to 2.8-fold for four of the seven target sites tested (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Refolding prior to embryo injection significantly increased the frequencies of pure PE for nine of 17 pegRNAs tested.
source: We found that refolding prior to embryo injection significantly increased the frequencies of pure PE (defined as the alleles containing only the pegRNA-specified edits without any other mutations) frequencies for nine of these 17 pegRNAs (Figure 2a and b).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2a and b.

claim: Pure PE is defined as the alleles containing only the pegRNA-specified edits without any other mutations.
source: We found that refolding prior to embryo injection significantly increased the frequencies of pure PE (defined as the alleles containing only the pegRNA-specified edits without any other mutations) frequencies for nine of these 17 pegRNAs (Figure 2a and b).
evidence: This is a definitional statement provided by the authors.

claim: Significant increases in pure PE were observed with seven of 12 pegRNAs designed to introduce base substitutions (increases ranging from 2.6- to 24.7-fold).
source: Significant increases were observed with seven of 12 pegRNAs designed to introduce base substitutions (increases ranging from 2.6- to 24.7-fold; Figure 2a) and 2 of 3 pegRNAs designed to create insertion pegRNAs (increases ranging from 1.7- to 4.6-fold; Figure 2b).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2a.

claim: Significant increases in pure PE were observed with 2 of 3 pegRNAs designed to create insertion pegRNAs (increases ranging from 1.7- to 4.6-fold).
source: Significant increases were observed with seven of 12 pegRNAs designed to introduce base substitutions (increases ranging from 2.6- to 24.7-fold; Figure 2a) and 2 of 3 pegRNAs designed to create insertion pegRNAs (increases ranging from 1.7- to 4.6-fold; Figure 2b).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2b.

claim: No significant increases in PE efficiencies were observed with the two pegRNAs designed to induce deletions.
source: We did not observe significant increases in PE efficiencies with the two pegRNAs designed to induce deletions (Figure 2b), perhaps due relatively lower degree of complementarity between the 5' spacer and 3' RTT because of the deletion encoded in the latter region.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2b.

claim: The lack of significant increases in PE efficiencies with deletion pegRNAs may be due to relatively lower degree of complementarity between the 5' spacer and 3' RTT because of the deletion encoded in the latter region.
source: We did not observe significant increases in PE efficiencies with the two pegRNAs designed to induce deletions (Figure 2b), perhaps due relatively lower degree of complementarity between the 5' spacer and 3' RTT because of the deletion encoded in the latter region.
evidence: This is a speculative explanation proposed by the authors for their observation.

claim: Increases in pure PE frequencies due to re-folding were accompanied by significant increases in non-pure PE frequencies.
source: In general, increases in pure PE frequencies due to re-folding were accompanied by significant increases in non-pure PE frequencies (Figure 2—figure supplement 1a, b) and therefore PE purity values (defined as the percentage of pure PE edits out of total edits) did not show significant differences for most of the pegRNAs we assessed (Figure 2—figure supplement 1c, d).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1a, b.

claim: PE purity is defined as the percentage of pure PE edits out of total edits.
source: In general, increases in pure PE frequencies due to re-folding were accompanied by significant increases in non-pure PE frequencies (Figure 2—figure supplement 1a, b) and therefore PE purity values (defined as the percentage of pure PE edits out of total edits) did not show significant differences for most of the pegRNAs we assessed (Figure 2—figure supplement 1c, d).
evidence: This is a definitional statement provided by the authors.

claim: PE purity values did not show significant differences for most of the pegRNAs assessed after refolding.
source: In general, increases in pure PE frequencies due to re-folding were accompanied by significant increases in non-pure PE frequencies (Figure 2—figure supplement 1a, b) and therefore PE purity values (defined as the percentage of pure PE edits out of total edits) did not show significant differences for most of the pegRNAs we assessed (Figure 2—figure supplement 1c, d).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1c, d.

claim: Two scn2b substitution pegRNAs showed significantly improved PE purities with re-folding.
source: The only exceptions were two scn2b substitution pegRNAs that actually showed significantly improved PE purities with re-folding and the cacng2b deletion pegRNA that showed significantly reduced PE purity with refolding (Figure 2—figure supplement 1c, d).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1c, d.

claim: The cacng2b deletion pegRNA showed significantly reduced PE purity with refolding.
source: The only exceptions were two scn2b substitution pegRNAs that actually showed significantly improved PE purities with re-folding and the cacng2b deletion pegRNA that showed significantly reduced PE purity with refolding (Figure 2—figure supplement 1c, d).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1c, d.

claim: PegRNAs harboring mutations at the RTT +1 and +2 positions could make PE more efficient than their unmutated pegRNA counterparts.
source: Following re-folding, complexation with PE2, and injection into zebrafish embryos, we found that pegRNAs harboring mutations at the RTT + 1 and+2 positions could make PE more efficient than their unmutated pegRNA counterparts (Figure 2c and Figure 2—figure supplement 2a).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2c and Figure 2—figure supplement 2a.

claim: A mutation at the RTT +2 position increased mean pure PE frequencies in all five cases tested.
source: Based on these results, we introduced a mutation at the RTT + 2 position in five additional pegRNAs specifying a single edit and found that the mutation increased mean pure PE frequencies in all five cases (Figure 2d).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2d.

claim: Three of the five mutated pegRNAs with RTT +2 mutations showed statistically significant increases in pure PE frequencies.
source: Three of the five mutated pegRNAs showed statistically significant increases in pure PE frequencies and two of these three pegRNAs also showed significant increases in non-pure PE frequencies (Figure 2d and Figure 2—figure supplement 2b).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2d.

claim: Two of the three pegRNAs with significant increases in pure PE frequencies also showed significant increases in non-pure PE frequencies.
source: Three of the five mutated pegRNAs showed statistically significant increases in pure PE frequencies and two of these three pegRNAs also showed significant increases in non-pure PE frequencies (Figure 2d and Figure 2—figure supplement 2b).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2d and Figure 2—figure supplement 2b.

claim: A mutation at the RTT +2 position increased pure PE frequency up to 6.7-fold (mean 2.4-fold).
source: Overall, a mutation at the RTT + 2 position increased pure PE frequency up to 6.7-fold (mean 2.4-fold; Figure 2c and d).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2c and d.

claim: PE purity was unchanged except for one pegRNA (cacng2b) that showed a modest but statistically significant increase with RTT +2 mutations.
source: PE purity was unchanged except for one pegRNA (cacng2b) that showed a modest but statistically significant increase (Figure 2—figure supplement 2c).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2c.

claim: Three re-folded pegRNAs harboring the RTT +2 mutations all induced higher indel frequencies with SpCas9 nuclease in zebrafish embryos than matched re-folded pegRNAs without the RTT +2 mutations.
source: Testing of three re-folded pegRNAs harboring the RTT + 2 mutations showed that they all induced higher indel frequencies with SpCas9 nuclease in zebrafish embryos than matched re-folded pegRNAs without the RTT + 2 mutations (Figure 2—figure supplement 3), suggesting that the +2 mutations function to enhance the abilities of these pegRNAs to form functional complexes with Cas9 protein.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3.

claim: The RTT +2 mutations function to enhance the abilities of pegRNAs to form functional complexes with Cas9 protein.
source: Testing of three re-folded pegRNAs harboring the RTT + 2 mutations showed that they all induced higher indel frequencies with SpCas9 nuclease in zebrafish embryos than matched re-folded pegRNAs without the RTT + 2 mutations (Figure 2—figure supplement 3), suggesting that the +2 mutations function to enhance the abilities of these pegRNAs to form functional complexes with Cas9 protein.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that RTT +2 mutations increase indel frequencies.

claim: Delivery of PE components as RNP complexes offers multiple potential advantages relative to DNA or RNA delivery (e.g. increased efficiency, reduced off-target effects, and avoiding risk of integration events).
source: Delivery of PE components as RNP complexes offers multiple potential advantages relative to DNA or RNA delivery (e.g. increased efficiency, reduced off-target effects, and avoiding risk of integration events; Kim et al., 2014; Raguram et al., 2022; Burger et al., 2016; Kanchiswamy, 2016; Svitashev et al., 2016; Wang et al., 2020; Ponnienselvan et al., 2023) and we show that combining pegRNA re-folding with the introduction of point mutations at the RTT +1 or+2 position can increase RNP-induced pure PE frequencies by as much as 29-fold in zebrafish embryos (Figure 1, Figure 2 and Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to prior work.

claim: Combining pegRNA re-folding with the introduction of point mutations at the RTT +1 or +2 position can increase RNP-induced pure PE frequencies by as much as 29-fold in zebrafish embryos.
source: Delivery of PE components as RNP complexes offers multiple potential advantages relative to DNA or RNA delivery (e.g. increased efficiency, reduced off-target effects, and avoiding risk of integration events; Kim et al., 2014; Raguram et al., 2022; Burger et al., 2016; Kanchiswamy, 2016; Svitashev et al., 2016; Wang et al., 2020; Ponnienselvan et al., 2023) and we show that combining pegRNA re-folding with the introduction of point mutations at the RTT +1 or+2 position can increase RNP-induced pure PE frequencies by as much as 29-fold in zebrafish embryos (Figure 1, Figure 2 and Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1, Figure 2 and Supplementary file 1.

claim: RNP-mediated PE functions in both zebrafish embryos and cultured human cells.
source: Our previous results showing that RNP-mediated PE functions in both zebrafish embryos and cultured human cells (Petri et al., 2022) suggest that these simple strategies should likely improve PE in other settings such as human and other cell types as well.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Petri et al., 2022.

claim: The simple strategies of pegRNA refolding and RTT mutations should likely improve PE in other settings such as human and other cell types.
source: Our previous results showing that RNP-mediated PE functions in both zebrafish embryos and cultured human cells (Petri et al., 2022) suggest that these simple strategies should likely improve PE in other settings such as human and other cell types as well.
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on prior results in zebrafish and human cells.

claim: The introduction of RTT mutations to reduce pegRNA 5' and 3' complementarity can be used when practicing PE technology using non-RNP-delivery methods such as DNA or RNA transfection, transduction, and/or injection.
source: The introduction of RTT mutations to reduce pegRNA 5' and 3' complementarity can also be used when practicing PE technology using non-RNP-delivery methods such as DNA or RNA transfection, transduction, and/or injection.
evidence: This is an inference about the applicability of the RTT mutation strategy to other delivery methods.

claim: Li et al., 2022 reported that introducing additional mutations in the RTT +1 to +3 positions can enhance PE efficiency in human cells via DNA transfection.
source: Notably, Li et al., 2022 have reported that introducing additional mutations in the RTT +1 to+3 positions can also enhance PE efficiency in human cells via DNA transfection.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Li et al., 2022.

claim: One important consideration in using the RTT mutation strategy is to ensure that the additional change introduced is either silent (if in a coding region) or otherwise benign in its effect.
source: One important consideration in using the RTT mutation strategy is to ensure that the additional change introduced is either silent (if in a coding region) or otherwise benign in its effect (Li et al., 2022).
evidence: This is a practical consideration supported by citation to Li et al., 2022.

claim: Ponnienselvan et al., 2023 reported that 3' truncated pegRNAs are preferentially loaded onto Cas9 and the prime editor protein, potentially due to reduced pegRNA 5'–3' interactions.
source: Corroborating our findings, Ponnienselvan et al., 2023 recently reported that 3' truncated pegRNAs are preferentially loaded onto Cas9 and the prime editor protein, potentially due to reduced pegRNA 5'–3' interactions.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Ponnienselvan et al., 2023.

claim: Adding various structured RNA motifs to the 3' termini of pegRNAs can improve PE efficiencies.
source: Although beyond the scope of this current work, it will be interesting to explore whether pegRNA re-folding and/or RTT mutation might be combined with other previously described strategies for improving PE efficiencies (e.g. adding various structured RNA motifs to the 3' termini of pegRNAs Nelson et al., 2022; Zhang et al., 2022 or PE proteins with improved architectures and activities Nelson et al., 2022; Doman et al., 2022; Liu et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Nelson et al., 2022 and Zhang et al., 2022.

claim: PE proteins with improved architectures and activities can improve PE efficiencies.
source: Although beyond the scope of this current work, it will be interesting to explore whether pegRNA re-folding and/or RTT mutation might be combined with other previously described strategies for improving PE efficiencies (e.g. adding various structured RNA motifs to the 3' termini of pegRNAs Nelson et al., 2022; Zhang et al., 2022 or PE proteins with improved architectures and activities Nelson et al., 2022; Doman et al., 2022; Liu et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Nelson et al., 2022; Doman et al., 2022; Liu et al., 2021.

claim: The length and base composition of pegRNA PBS and RTT sequences can influence PE efficiency for any given target spacer site.
source: Previous work has shown that the length and base composition of pegRNA PBS and RTT sequences can influence PE efficiency for any given target spacer site (Ponnienselvan et al., 2023; Kim et al., 2021; Li et al., 2021; Lin et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to prior work.

claim: Internal complementarity between the 5' spacer and 3' PBS/RTT regions of the pegRNA is an additional parameter to be considered when designing and testing various combinations to optimize PE activity.
source: Our work adds another parameter (internal complementarity between the 5' spacer and 3' PBS/RTT regions of the pegRNA) to be considered as one designs and tests various combinations to optimize PE activity.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental findings of this study.

claim: Accounting for internal complementarity may impact the nature of spacer sequences that can efficiently be targeted (e.g. higher GC content and/or melting temperature may actually be undesirable).
source: Accounting for this additional consideration may impact the nature of spacer sequences that can efficiently be targeted (e.g. higher GC content and/or melting temperature may actually be undesirable) and the length and composition of PBS/RTT sequences that can be used.
evidence: This is a speculative inference about the implications of the findings.

claim: Accounting for internal complementarity may impact the length and composition of PBS/RTT sequences that can be used.
source: Accounting for this additional consideration may impact the nature of spacer sequences that can efficiently be targeted (e.g. higher GC content and/or melting temperature may actually be undesirable) and the length and composition of PBS/RTT sequences that can be used.
evidence: This is a speculative inference about the implications of the findings.

claim: The generation of larger datasets of optimized pegRNAs and consideration of all parameters that can influence pegRNA activities (including internal complementarity) may yield improved rules and software for in silico design in the future.
source: We envision that the generation of larger datasets of optimized pegRNAs and consideration of all the parameters that can influence pegRNA activities (including internal complementarity) may yield improved rules and software for in silico design in the future.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about future directions.

claim: The DNA templates for in vitro transcription were constructed by one-step PCR, using a C9E constant oligonucleotide containing the enhanced SpCas9 scaffold.
source: The DNA templates for in vitro transcription were constructed by one-step PCR, using a C9E constant oligonucleotide containing the enhanced SpCas9 scaffold (Petri et al., 2022), forward primer carrying the SP6 promoter and target-specific spacer, and the reverse primer with the 3' extension containing the primer binding site and RTT.
evidence: This is a methodological description supported by citation to Petri et al., 2022.

claim: PegRNAs in water were refolded by heating at 98 °C for 2 min and slowly cooling down at a rate of –0.1 °C per second to 30 °C.
source: PegRNAs in water were refolded by heating at 98 °C for 2 min and slowly cooling down at a rate of –0.1 °C per second to 30 °C.
evidence: This is a methodological description of the refolding procedure.

claim: Refolded pegRNAs were immediately added to the SpCas9 or PE2 protein, mixed gently, and followed by a 10 min incubation at 30 °C.
source: Refolded pegRNAs were immediately added to the SpCas9 or PE2 protein, mixed gently, spun for 10 s at 6000 RPM in a mini centrifuge (Fisherbrand), and followed by a 10 min incubation at 30 °C.
evidence: This is a methodological description of the RNP complexation procedure.

claim: All zebrafish husbandry and experiments were approved by the Massachusetts General Hospital Subcommittee on Research Animal Care and performed under the guidelines of the Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee at the Massachusetts General Hospital (Protocol #2005N000025).
source: All zebrafish (Danio rerio) husbandry and experiments were approved by the Massachusetts General Hospital Subcommittee on Research Animal Care and performed under the guidelines of the Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee at the Massachusetts General Hospital (Protocol #2005N000025).
evidence: This is a statement about ethical approval for the research.
